Print, summarise and tidy a lag sequential analysis fit

Source: R/lsa.R, R/methods-lsa.R
lsa-methods.Rd

print(), summary(), as.data.frame() and nobs() describe a fitted lag sequential analysis, an lsa object from lsa(). A fit has three levels of description: the model as a whole (its size and the tablewise test of independence), the states (how often each is left and entered, and how often a sequence starts in it), and the individual transitions. These methods give the first two levels; transitions() gives the third.

print() shows a compact overview: the engine and lag, the numbers of states, transitions, events and sequences, the likelihood-ratio test of independence, the number of significant transitions out of the cells tested (a structural zero, such as a self-transition with loops = FALSE, has no p-value and is not counted), the strongest over-represented transitions and the initial-state distribution. summary() returns a summary.lsa object holding two tables, a one-row overview of the fit and one row per state, which are read with as.data.frame(summary(fit), what = ). For a grouped fit, summary() returns one overview row per group. as.data.frame() on a fit returns the full edge table, including the integer state ids and the network columns that transitions() leaves out. nobs() is the number of transitions the model was fitted to.

For the per-transition, per-state and per-test tables, prefer the reading verbs transitions(), nodes(), tests() and initial().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.lsa'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.lsa'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("overview", "nodes"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
nobs(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ). For print() and as.data.frame() on a summary, a summary.lsa object.

...

Ignored.

row.names

Optional row names for the returned data frame; ignored by the grouped method.

optional

Ignored; present for consistency with the generic.

what

For as.data.frame() on a summary: "overview" (default, the one-row overview of the fit) or "nodes" (one row per state).

Value

  • print() returns x invisibly.

  • summary() on an lsa fit returns an object of class summary.lsa holding two tables. The overview has one row and the columns engine, lag, n_states, n_sequences, n_events, n_transitions, n_significant, alpha, lrx2, lrx2_df, lrx2_p, x2, x2_df, x2_p (NA where the engine computed no tablewise test or the input was a transition matrix). The node table has one row per state and the columns state, outgoing, incoming, out_share, in_share, init_prob. Read them with as.data.frame(s) and as.data.frame(s, what = "nodes").

  • summary() on a grouped fit returns a data.frame with one row per group: a leading group column followed by the overview columns.

  • as.data.frame() on an lsa fit returns a data.frame with one row per from -> to cell: integer from and to ids, from_label, to_label, the statistic columns of transitions(), and the network columns edge and weight. On a grouped fit the tables are stacked under a leading group column.

  • as.data.frame() on a summary returns the overview or the node table.

  • nobs() returns a single number, the total transition count.

See also

lsa(); transitions(), nodes(), tests() and initial() for the reading verbs.

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
fit
#> Lag Sequential Analysis  -  classical  (lag 1, directed)
#>   3 states | 1734 transitions | 1870 events | 136 sequences
#>   states: Active, Average, Disengaged
#>   independence: G² = 618.3, df = 4, p <2e-16
#> 
#>   Significant transitions (p < 0.05): 7 of 9
#>   strongest over-represented (of 3):
#>     Active -> Active          z =  +21.7  ***
#>     Disengaged -> Disengaged  z =  +15.4  ***
#>     Average -> Average        z =  +12.5  ***
#> 
#>   Initial states:
#>     Active     0.382  ████████████████████████
#>     Average    0.368  ███████████████████████
#>     Disengaged 0.250  ████████████████
s <- summary(fit)
s
#> Lag sequential analysis: classical engine, lag 1
#>   3 states, 1734 transitions, 1870 events, 136 sequences
#>   significant transitions (p < 0.05): 7 of 9
#>   likelihood-ratio test: G² = 618.31, df = 4, p <2e-16
#>   Pearson test: χ² = 629.20, df = 4, p <2e-16
#> 
#>   State activity (share of transitions out and in):
#>     Active      out 0.379 ██████████    in 0.375 ██████████
#>     Average     out 0.433 ████████████  in 0.440 ████████████
#>     Disengaged  out 0.187 █████         in 0.185 █████
as.data.frame(s)
#>      engine lag n_states n_sequences n_events n_transitions n_significant alpha
#> 1 classical   1        3         136     1870          1734             7  0.05
#>       lrx2 lrx2_df       lrx2_p       x2 x2_df          x2_p
#> 1 618.3053       4 1.69152e-132 629.2022     4 7.406567e-135
as.data.frame(s, what = "nodes")
#>        state outgoing incoming out_share  in_share init_prob
#> 1     Active      658      651 0.3794694 0.3754325 0.3823529
#> 2    Average      751      763 0.4331027 0.4400231 0.3676471
#> 3 Disengaged      325      320 0.1874279 0.1845444 0.2500000
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 1734
head(as.data.frame(fit))
#>   from to from_label to_label lag count expected      prob   prob_col
#> 1    1  1     Active   Active   1   459 247.0346 0.6975684 0.70506912
#> 2    2  1    Average   Active   1   153 281.9498 0.2037284 0.23502304
#> 3    3  1 Disengaged   Active   1    39 122.0156 0.1200000 0.05990783
#> 4    1  2     Active  Average   1   176 289.5352 0.2674772 0.23066841
#> 5    2  2    Average  Average   1   458 330.4573 0.6098535 0.60026212
#> 6    3  2 Disengaged  Average   1   129 143.0075 0.3969231 0.16906946
#>      adj_res             p    yules_q      kappa    kappa_z      kappa_p
#> 1  21.662811 4.602765e-104  0.8278779  0.4438330  19.187756 4.684307e-82
#> 2 -12.906038  4.161672e-38 -0.6010580 -0.4994042 -14.696262 6.811736e-49
#> 3 -10.549486  5.107575e-26 -0.6983917 -0.7069460 -11.462654 2.031922e-30

gfit <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
            time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
gfit
#> <lsa_group>
#>   engine:    classical
#>   states:    9 (adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan, synthesis)
#>   groups:    2
#>     - High:        1000 sequences
#>     - Low:         1000 sequences
summary(gfit)
#>   group    engine lag n_states n_sequences n_events n_transitions n_significant
#> 1  High classical   1        9        1000    13721         12721            66
#> 2   Low classical   1        9        1000    13812         12812            67
#>   alpha     lrx2 lrx2_df lrx2_p       x2 x2_df x2_p
